desc:
The strings a and b each hold a non-negative integer written in binary. Return their sum, also as a binary string.

The result must not have leading zeros unless it is exactly "0". The inputs can be far longer than any built-in integer type, so do the addition yourself, digit by digit.

For example, "11" + "1" gives "100", and "1010" + "1011" gives "10101".
constraints: a and b contain only the characters 0 and 1
Neither string has leading zeros, except for the string "0" itself
hints: Add the way you do on paper: start from the rightmost digits and move left, remembering a carry.
At every position the digit sum is bitA + bitB + carry, which is between 0 and 3. The new digit is that sum modulo 2, and the new carry is the sum divided by 2.
Keep going while either string has digits left or the carry is non-zero. Collect the digits in a list and reverse it at the end instead of prepending to a string.
editorial: Use two pointers starting at the last character of each string and a carry initialised to 0. In each step add the current digit of each string (treating an exhausted string as 0) plus the carry. Append sum % 2 to the output and set carry = sum // 2. When both strings are exhausted and the carry is zero, reverse the collected digits to get the answer.

Because both inputs have no leading zeros, the result never has them either, except that "0"+"0" yields a single "0". Converting to integers and back is not allowed in spirit here: the point is the digit-by-digit procedure, which runs in O(max(n, m)) time and works for numbers of any size.
solution:
def addBinary(a, b):
    i, j = len(a) - 1, len(b) - 1
    carry = 0
    out = []
    while i >= 0 or j >= 0 or carry:
        total = carry
        if i >= 0:
            total += ord(a[i]) - 48
            i -= 1
        if j >= 0:
            total += ord(b[j]) - 48
            j -= 1
        out.append(chr(48 + total % 2))
        carry = total // 2
    out.reverse()
    return "".join(out) if out else "0"
